extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners referencing MPEP guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining and applying 35 U.S.C. 102 (a)-(g) rejections, including how to determine prior-art dates for references (especially those based on international applications), when provisional 102(e) rejections are appropriate, and which form paragraphs to use in Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(e) prior-art date for international applications published in English (filed on/after Nov 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: All references (WIPO publication, U.S. patent application publication, or U.S. patent of, or claiming the benefit of, an international application (IA) filed on or after November 29, 2000, designated the U.S., and published in English under PCT Article 21(2)) have the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date of the international filing date or earlier effective U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No benefit of the international filing date (nor any U.S. filing dates prior to the IA) is given for 35 U.S.C. 102(e) purposes if the IA was published under PCT Article 21(2) by WIPO in a language other than English. Use form paragraph 7.12 where applicable; consider priority/benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisionals/nonprovisionals or internationals only if support exists (see 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120).

rubrics_metrics.name: IA publication in non-English language — no 102(e) benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application was published by WIPO in a language other than English, the international filing date is not given as a U.S. filing date for prior art purposes under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In that case the IA publication by WIPO may be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date; U.S. patent or U.S. publication may have 102(e) dates based on actual U.S. filing dates. See form paragraphs 7.08 and 7.09 for applying under 102(a)/(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of additional priority/benefit claims for 102(e) dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IA properly claimed priority to an earlier-filed U.S. provisional (35 U.S.C. 119(e)) or an earlier-filed U.S. nonprovisional (35 U.S.C. 120) application, the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date for references may be the filing date of the earlier-filed U.S. application, assuming proper support is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date, consider priority/benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisional and nonprovisional applications and internationals under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121 or 365(c) only if the subject matter used to make the rejection is appropriately supported in the relied-upon earlier-filed application's disclosure (and any intermediate application(s)). Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) and 365(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(e) date for U.S. publication/patent when IA not published in English (filed on/after Nov 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an IA filed on or after November 29, 2000 was not published in English under PCT Article 21(2), the U.S. publication and U.S. patent of the 35 U.S.C. 111(a) continuation have the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date of the actual U.S. filing date of the 111(a) application; the IA publication by WIPO has no 102(e)(1) date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IA publication by WIPO can be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date. If additional priority/benefit claims exist to earlier-filed U.S. apps, the 102(e) date for the U.S. publication/patent remains the actual filing date of the later-filed 111(a) application unless proper support yields an earlier effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(e) treatment for international applications filed prior to Nov 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IA was filed prior to November 29, 2000 (so AIPA amendments do not apply), the U.S. publication and U.S. patent of a 111(a) continuation (filed prior to any entry of the national stage) have the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date of their actual U.S. filing date; the IA publication under PCT Article 21(2) does not have a prior art date under 102(e)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such IA publications may be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of their publication date. Use pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rules (form paragraph 7.12.01) when the reference is a U.S. patent resulting from an IA filed before Nov 29, 2000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pre-AIPA vs post-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The changes made to 35 U.S.C. 102(e) by the American Inventors Protection Act (AIPA) and the 2002 amendments do not apply when the reference is a U.S. patent resulting directly or indirectly from an IA filed before November 29, 2000; in that situation apply pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (form paragraph 7.12.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference is a U.S. patent issued directly from a national stage of such IA, the reference's 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date is the date the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1), (2) and (4) were fulfilled. Caution that the WIPO publication may have an earlier prior art date under 102(a) or 102(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejections — when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: If an earlier-filed, copending, and unpublished U.S. patent application discloses subject matter which would anticipate the claims in a later-filed pending U.S. application that has a different inventive entity, the examiner should determine whether a provisional 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection of the later-filed application can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional 102(e) rejection is appropriate where the earlier-filed application is not published at time of rejection; the rejection is based on a presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application. Use form paragraph 7.15.01 when making a provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions required for provisional 102(e) rejection (common inventor/assignee & different effective filing dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) should be made if (1) at least one common inventor exists between the applications or the applications are commonly assigned and (2) the effective filing dates are different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copending application must have either a common assignee or at least one common inventor. The provisional rejection is premised on the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the copending application which would constitute prior art under 102(e) if published or patented.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to overcome a provisional 102(e) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional 102(e) rejection may be overcome by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the copending application was derived from the inventor of the instant application (i.e., not the invention 'by another'), or by an appropriate showing under 37 CFR 1.131; or by abandoning applications and filing a new application containing the subject matter of both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection may NOT be overcome by the filing of a terminal disclaimer (see In re Bartfeld). Provide appropriate evidence or admissions as needed. Use form paragraph 7.15.01 text and examiner notes to explain grounds and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional double patenting and related rejections when claims conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claims of the copending application conflict with the claims of the instant application, a provisional double patenting rejection should also be given using form paragraphs 8.30 and 8.32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, if evidence shows either invention is prior art unto the other under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) or (g), make rejections using form paragraphs 7.13 and/or 7.14 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality prevents relying on unpublished copending application without common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no common assignee or inventor and the application was not published pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b), the confidential status of applications under 35 U.S.C. 122(a) must be maintained and no rejection can be made relying on the earlier-filed, unpublished application as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing dates of the applications are within 6 months (3 months for simple subject matter), interference may be proper (see MPEP Chapter 2300). If the earliest-filed application will not be published under 122(b), it must be allowed to issue once statutory requirements are met; after patenting it may be used as a 102(e) reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(f) — applicant not the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(f) bars the issuance of a patent where an applicant did not invent the subject matter being claimed and sought to be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must presume applicants are the proper inventors unless there is proof that another made the invention and that applicant derived the invention from the true inventor. See MPEP §§ 2137 - 2137.02 for substantive requirements and procedures for 102(f) rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(g) — priority of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(g) bars issuance of a patent where another made the invention in the United States before applicant and had not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed it; this section forms a basis for interference practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining priority under 102(g) consider dates of conception and reduction to practice and the reasonable diligence of the parties (first to conceive and last to reduce to practice). See MPEP Chapter 2300 and §§ 2138 - 2138.06 for interference procedures and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and sequencing of form paragraphs (7.07–7.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.07 to 7.17 are to be used when making rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102; particular paragraphs must be preceded by others (for example, 7.07 often must precede 7.08–7.14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 7.07 (Statement of Statutory Basis) is required in first actions on the merits and final rejections; elsewhere form paragraph 7.103 may be used. Specific paragraphs include 7.08 (102(a)), 7.09 (102(b)), 7.10 (102(c)), 7.11 (102(d)), 7.12/7.12.01 (102(e)), 7.13 (102(f)), 7.14 (102(g)), 7.15 variants (combined 102(a),(b),(g) and 102(e) usages). Follow the 'Examiner Note' instructions for correct ordering and combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.12 — 102(e) rejection rules under AIPA and 2002 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.12 sets out the text of 102(e) as amended by AIPA and the 2002 Act and specifies that this paragraph should be used only if the reference is (a) filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), or (b) a U.S. patent issued directly or indirectly from, or a U.S. or WIPO publication of, an international application with an international filing date on or after November 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining the 102(e) date, consider priority/benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisionals, nonprovisionals, and internationals only if support exists; DO NOT consider foreign priority claims under 119(a)-(d) and 365(a). If conditions for relying on an international filing date are not met, apply the reference under 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.12.01 — 102(e) rejection when reference derives from IA filed prior to Nov 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.12.01 is to be used when the reference is a U.S. patent issued directly or indirectly from a national stage of, or a continuing application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 365(c) to, an international application having an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this situation, pre-AIPA 102(e) is applicable. If the reference is a U.S. patent issued directly from a national stage, the reference's 102(e) date is the date the requirements of 371(c)(1), (2) and (4) were fulfilled. Consider priority/benefit claims only as permitted and only when supported by the relied-upon disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for 102(e) rejections distinguishing common vs no common assignee/inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ¶7.15.02 for 102(e) rejections where the applied reference has a common assignee or inventor with the instant application; use ¶7.15.03 when there is no common assignee or inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶7.15.02 explains that the applied reference constitutes prior art under 102(e) based on earlier effective U.S. filing date and lists how to overcome (37 CFR 1.132 or 1.131). ¶7.15.03 is used to reject over a patent or patent application publication with earlier filing date that discloses invention but need not have a common assignee/inventor. Both paragraphs must be preceded by appropriate other form paragraphs (e.g., 7.07 and either 7.12 or 7.12.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.16 — 102(b) public use or on sale rejections (evidence requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) based upon a public use or sale of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.07 and 7.09 or by form paragraph 7.103. A full explanation of the evidence establishing a public use or sale must be provided in the action (bracketed text).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.17 — 102(c) abandonment rejections (evidence requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) because the invention has been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07 and 7.10 or by form paragraph 7.103. Evidence establishing abandonment of the invention should be supplied (see MPEP § 2134).
